title: TCGA held-out test set performance
notes: Performance is evaluated on 1,681 patients across 27 tumor classes. All five metrics use 2,000 bootstrap replicates.
Percentile confidence intervals use patient bootstrap resampling within true cancer class, preserving observed class counts and the fixed classifier and panel (Methods).
AUROC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; CI, confidence interval; TCGA, The Cancer Genome Atlas.

title: External primary-tumor performance and matched original-prediction comparison
notes: Primary matched macro-F1 uses the fixed 26-class shared axis (25 truth classes present).
Original predictions are retained, including MiniCpG ESCA/STAD assignments. Full and matched subsets have different membership.
Confidence intervals: 2,000 percentile bootstrap resamples of known patient groups, stratified by unit truth-class signature; unidentified specimens are separate units.

Patient-balanced estimates give each patient unit equal total weight: each specimen receives the inverse of the number of that unit’s included specimens in the evaluated subset. Specimens without patient identifiers form separate units. Bootstrap draws multiply these fixed subset weights by the sampled unit multiplicity.
AUROC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; CI, confidence interval. Full-cohort macro-F1 uses the fixed model-class axis; matched macro-F1 uses the fixed shared axis.

title: Matched comparisons under original and reassigned predictions
notes: Original MiniCpG predictions are principal. Runner-up changes only ESCA/STAD predictions to the highest-probability remaining class, without retraining or changing specimens.

Both policies reuse identical bootstrap draws. Differences and confidence intervals are in percentage points (MiniCpG minus MethyDeep). Primary macro-F1 has a fixed 26-class axis; domains use represented truth classes.
AUROC is unchanged by output reassignment because probability scores are unchanged. Specimen-weighted results are principal; patient-balanced estimates are complementary.

Patient-balanced estimates give each patient unit equal total weight: each specimen receives the inverse of the number of that unit’s included specimens in the evaluated subset. Specimens without patient identifiers form separate units. Bootstrap draws multiply these fixed subset weights by the sampled unit multiplicity.

title: Panel-size sensitivity comparing MiniCpG K20 with MethyDeep
notes: Both classifiers used 3,496 matched primary-tumor samples across 25 represented classes. MiniCpG K20 uses 20 CpGs; MethyDeep uses 30. Differences are MiniCpG K20 minus MethyDeep and are reported in percentage points (pp); the source proportion differences equal pp/100.

The K=20 model was evaluated only as a panel-size sensitivity analysis. Both classifiers were evaluated on identical matched samples with their original predictions unchanged. MiniCpG refers to the locked K=30 model, selected during development.
Final eligibility refresh, 10 November 2026; K20 comparison and uncertainty tables.
Paired confidence intervals use 2,000 bootstrap replicates. AUROC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; CI, confidence interval.

title: Consensus and single-split panel performance
notes: All 101 panels contain 30 CpGs; each was fitted using 10 matched classifier seeds and evaluated on the same 3,186 primary-tumor samples with at most 5 missing CpGs per panel.
Macro-F1 uses the fixed 27-class model axis, including zero scores for classes absent from this common subset (TCGA-KIRP, TCGA-TGCT). Other metric definitions are provided in Figure 2.
The common subset retains 3,186 of 3,683 primary samples and represents 25 tumor classes. Coverage requirements were applied identically to all panels.

Confidence intervals use 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates of known patient groups, stratified by each group’s set of truth classes. Specimens without patient identifiers form separate units; resampling is identical across all panels and seeds.

Selection-frequency association includes single-split panels only, using fixed development-derived frequencies. The bootstrap resamples evaluation samples, not panels. Panels share probes and are not independent biological replications.

Selection frequency is the fraction of the original development folds selecting each CpG. Panel mean frequency averages these fractions across its 30 CpGs. Seed SD describes classifier randomness, not a confidence interval.
This post hoc analysis did not change the locked panel or classifier configuration. Intervals condition on the fitted models, fixed panels and evaluated cohort.
Source: final eligibility refresh, 10 November 2026, fixed-panel ten-seed analysis.

title: Tumor purity and classification errors in the TCGA held-out test set

blocks.title: Purity estimates were matched to methylation specimens using file UUIDs, GDC sample metadata and the first 16 characters of ABSOLUTE sample barcodes (patient, sample type and vial). Matching does not establish identical aliquots or tissue sections. Predictions were taken from the unchanged locked MiniCpG classifier.

title: Primary-tumor recognition by source study and class
notes: Recall is the fraction of specimens of a true class correctly classified. Wilson intervals are descriptive 95% binomial intervals; specimens within a study may not be independent.
All eligible source–class groups are included, including small groups. Patient-unit counts use available identifiers; unknown rows remain separate units. No minimum sample-size threshold was applied.
COAD/READ and ESCA/STAD denote the merged classifier classes. Source links point to public study records.

title: Directed confusions and class-pair methylation similarity
notes: Directed error rate = specimens assigned to the destination class / specimens of the true class in that source. Only observed directions are listed in the first block.
Pooled pair confusion rate = (A assigned to B + B assigned to A) / (number of A + number of B). All pairs of externally represented classes are included in the second block.

Similarity = 1 − (distance − minimum distance) / (maximum distance − minimum distance), using all pairwise Euclidean distances between external class mean beta profiles, with frozen training-median imputation.

title: Within-class methylation dispersion in the TCGA development set
notes: The class centroid is the mean beta vector across the MiniCpG probes. Each specimen’s dispersion is its Euclidean distance to its own class mean centroid.
The class summary is the median specimen-to-centroid distance; Q1 and Q3 describe the specimen-distance distribution. Rank 1 indicates the greatest median dispersion.
The frozen training-median missing-value policy is retained. Development data are used only as the reference; this table does not report development prediction performance.

title: Aggregate sarcoma and uveal melanoma source annotations
notes: Histological and reported methylation-cluster categories are source annotations, not new eligibility rules or proof of molecular-subtype coverage.
Within a source/cohort and annotation field, categories with fewer than five specimens are pooled for reporting; analytical membership and predictions are unchanged.
No patient/specimen identifiers, individual predictions or linked BAP1/chromosome annotations are included. Development-set performance is not reported.
Unknown or ambiguous annotations remain in the denominators. Source references identify studies, not individual specimens.

title: Uveal melanoma–cutaneous melanoma study geometry and probe missingness
notes: All full-panel distances are Euclidean distances between mean beta profiles using frozen training-median imputation. Dispersion is the median specimen distance to the relevant source/class mean centroid.

Observed-dimension diagnostics omit probes absent from a study and project both reference centroids onto the same remaining probes. They are descriptive diagnostics, not rerun classifier predictions or evidence that imputation caused the errors.

The missing-probe squared-shift fraction sums per-probe contributions over missing dimensions; it is not applicable to the development reference itself. Geometry cannot establish subtype coverage or isolate biological effects.

title: External study sources, eligibility and cohort coverage
notes: Counts summarize the curated external inventory. Cohorts overlap; totals must not be added as independent specimens.
Primary eligibility is fixed separately. Metastatic, FFPE and EPIC eligibility is assessed independently using the rules in Methods.
Evaluated counts additionally require adopted beta availability and model-specific panel coverage. Shared comparisons require reference labels supported by both models.
Study characteristics summarize the source inventory and do not imply identical preservation, platform or processing for every specimen. No individual identifiers or linked annotations are included.

title: Expanded-cohort original-prediction performance
notes: Primary matched macro-F1 uses the fixed 26-class shared axis (25 truth classes present). Expanded-domain macro-F1 uses the truth classes present in each evaluated subset.
Original predictions are retained, including MiniCpG ESCA/STAD assignments. Full and matched subsets have different membership. Expanded cohorts overlap.
Confidence intervals: 2,000 percentile bootstrap resamples of known patient groups, stratified by unit truth-class signature; unidentified specimens are separate units.

Patient-balanced estimates give each patient unit equal total weight: each specimen receives the inverse of the number of that unit’s included specimens in the evaluated subset. Specimens without patient identifiers form separate units. Bootstrap draws multiply these fixed subset weights by the sampled unit multiplicity.

title: Class- and study-level performance and cohort overlap
notes: Original MiniCpG predictions. Cohort-specific summaries retain each cohort membership; Fig. 5B summaries count each specimen once across the three expanded cohorts.
Mixed denotes a study–class group containing more than one membership combination. Study consistency is descriptive; small groups have considerable uncertainty.
Overlap and independent-evidence counts prevent shared specimens from being interpreted as independent replication. Primary results are retained as context.

Recall intervals are descriptive 95% Wilson binomial intervals based on specimen counts. They do not account for within-patient or within-study dependence; patient-unit and unknown-identity counts expose available support. Overlapping cohorts are not independent.

title: Controlled clinical and input-processing comparisons
notes: Clinical differences: lymph node minus primary, equally weighted by patient. Processing differences: alternative minus evaluated author-supplied workflow, equally weighted by paired specimen.
Fig. 5E reverses the GSE144487 export comparison to display normalized minus non-normalized; source-direction and plotted-direction estimates are both retained below.
Intervals use 20,000 paired bootstrap draws. Small or zero changes do not establish equivalence; conservative bounds are provided when empirical intervals are unstable or degenerate.

title: Genomic annotation of the MiniCpG consensus panel
notes: GRCh38/hg38 coordinates follow the source manifest: start is 0-based and end is exclusive (the corresponding 1-based final base). Each interval spans the two-base CpG dinucleotide.
Unique genes are listed in full. Transcript-associated gene entries may repeat; their signed distances to transcription start sites (TSS), in base pairs, correspond positionally to the next column.
CGI denotes CpG island. The CGI identifier and island/shore/shelf context are retained from the manifest; open sea indicates no annotated island context. NA denotes an unavailable annotation.

Source: NCI GDC HM450.hg38.manifest.gencode.v36.tsv; https://gdc.cancer.gov/about-data/gdc-data-processing/gdc-reference-files. Coordinate definitions: https://zwdzwd.github.io/InfiniumAnnotation/manifest.html.

title: Tumor–normal methylation shifts for MiniCpG probes
notes: Development and held-out tumor summaries use the corresponding tumor subsets. Normal-reference means/medians can recur across subsets. Beta differences are tumor minus normal; values are unitless.

title: Tumor-versus-normal-adjacent signal-check performance
notes: 95% confidence intervals use 20,000 patient-cluster bootstrap resamples, stratified by TCGA project and available specimen types. Matched tumor/normal specimens remain together; models and thresholds are fixed. AUROC and AUPRC are threshold-independent. These results concern normal-adjacent tissue, not healthy or benign-disease screening specificity.

AUROC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; AUPRC, area under the precision–recall curve. TP/FP/TN/FN denote true positive, false positive, true negative and false negative classifications. Performance and confidence limits are proportions; the decision threshold is on the model-specific score scale.

Training samples: 4,899 tumors and 543 normal-adjacent specimens. Held-out samples: 1,217 tumors and 170 normal-adjacent specimens across 14 represented TCGA classes. Threshold selection repeats: 200.
Thresholds use repeated calibration at each target sensitivity and the median threshold across repeats; rules and exact settings are given in Supplementary Methods SM6.
Secondary TCGA tumor versus normal-adjacent signal check using the locked 30-CpG panel; not healthy no-cancer or benign-disease specificity.

title: Continuous probe-level biological scores and supporting measurements
notes: Lineage, tumor–normal shift and tumor-composition scores are complementary continuous summaries. They do not assign mutually exclusive biological categories or establish mechanisms.
Percentiles and scores are on a 0–1 scale. The normal–tumor lineage correlation uses pooled TCGA development set and held-out class medians, as specified in Methods.

title: Paired tumor and normal-adjacent substitution outcomes
notes: The same 147 patient pairs and cancer labels were evaluated in both conditions with the locked MiniCpG classifier and CpG panel.
Normal-substituted inputs contain matched normal-adjacent beta values; correctness is evaluated against the patient’s tumor class.
Both correct: correct in both conditions; lost: tumor only correct; recovered: substituted only correct; both wrong: neither correct.
Intervals use 20,000 paired patient bootstrap resamples within cancer type. Difference is normal-substituted minus tumor accuracy. Individual records are not redistributed.

title: Within-class purity and immune association summaries
notes: Spearman ρ and absolute ρ are reported without causal interpretation. Composition breadth counts associations meeting the displayed absolute-correlation threshold and minimum sample count. Project-specific and class-centered summaries are separate analyses.

Class-centered correlations subtract within-project means from methylation and covariates before pooled Spearman correlation. They differ from within-project composition-score correlations. Descriptive category labels follow the thresholds and sequential rules in Supplementary Methods SM6; they do not establish causal categories.

title: Methylation–expression associations and transcriptome ranks
notes: Project-matched specimens count the project-level methylation–expression overlap. Specimens used in correlation exclude missing beta values for that CpG; this is the sample size for the reported Spearman test.
Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) q-values are calculated separately for each CpG × TCGA project across all tested genes, before selecting the annotated gene associations shown here.
Transcriptome ranks and percentiles compare absolute Spearman ρ with all tested genes for the same CpG and project. These ranks are distinct from the Spearman p-value and its BH correction.
The current panel contributes 23 annotated probes. Genes without usable expression in a project are absent; remaining panel probes have no linked gene annotation.

title: Exploratory cfDNA-native compact-panel analysis
notes: SDs and repeat ranges describe variation across evaluated splits; they are not confidence intervals because training sets overlap and specimens recur across repeats. Subtype metrics condition on each workflow’s own detected cancers.
Differences are descriptive; subtype-evaluation subsets differ between workflows. Differences and SDs are on the proportion scale (e.g., 0.01 = 1 percentage point).
Cancer-type confusion cells are row percentages.

title: Protocol-informed cost estimate for a proposed targeted MiniCpG assay

blocks.title: Standalone batch: 96 patient samples, 16 controls and 2 sequencing runs. Quantities are derived from the specified workflow; sources refer to price anchors, not validation of every assumed quantity.
Standalone batch: 96 patient samples, 16 controls and 2 sequencing runs. Quantities are derived from the specified workflow; sources refer to price anchors, not validation of every assumed quantity.

The following is a planning schedule for an established assay, not a measured MiniCpG turnaround. The reference batch comprises 88 patients and 8 controls. Hands-on allowances come from the same cost model; incubation times come from protocols where available. Incubations and staff time can overlap and must not simply be added across every sample.

For an explicit calendar example, Day 1 starts at 08:00. Conversion and target PCR are scheduled on Day 1, with products held for cleanup if necessary; cleanup, library preparation and QC finish by 16:00 on Day 2. The two-day preparation schedule is an assumption requiring sufficient equipment and staffing. Three 96-well thermal blocks, two available sequencing instruments for the standalone batch, concurrent library processing and immediate access to QC instruments are assumed. Bench staff work eight-hour days; instruments run overnight. No weekend or holiday interruption is imposed.

title: Age representation across development and evaluation cohorts
notes: Paediatric: below 18 years; adult: at least 18 years. Unknown denotes absent or uninterpretable age metadata. Cohorts overlap.
Counts use the original MiniCpG-evaluable specimens. Age categories incorporate source clinical metadata and unambiguous age bands; exact ages are not inferred from bands.
